newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs seen rising to and above 124.00.
newsitem.headline: JGBs seen rising to and above 124.00.

text.p: The key September 10-year Japanese government bond (JGB) futures contract could rise to and above 124.00 on Thursday after rising as high as 123.91 on LIFFE on Wednesday.
The contract finished Tokyo at 123.74 on Wednesday.
Operators are likely to continue covering short positions they built earlier for hedging because the yen's rise against the dollar is expected to hinder a recovery in Japan's economy.
"It seems that people who had expected a rise in Japanese interest rates between July and September had all changed their minds by Wednesday," said a dealer at a securities house.
"We should see if the yen's strength is temporary and whether the Nikkei (stock average) falls below the key 20,000 level. But in a short-run, the market is bullish," he said.
Traders said the September's downside room seemed to be limited at 123.50 after cash bond buying, apparently from public funds, boosted it beyond that level on Wednesday.
But rises could be curbed as some remain cautious ahead of the Bank of Japan's "tankan" survey due out on June 25.
"Investors' pre-tankan buying may stop for now because their target of 2.4 percent for the key 182nd 10-year JGBs was cleared on Wednesday," said another brokerage house dealer.
